How Restaurants in Italy Should Manage Google Reviews

By RMA — Web Reputation Agency

Restaurant Google reviews follow patterns of their own: high volume, strong seasonality, a mix of tourists and regulars, and a recurring risk of customers who threaten a bad review in exchange for a free meal. Managing them well in Italy means knowing which reviews can be reported, replying in a way that reassures the next guest, and building a steady flow of genuine feedback.

What makes restaurant reviews different

For a restaurant, Google is often the first and only place a guest checks before booking, and reviews there are more detailed than for most other businesses. Google asks diners to rate food, service and atmosphere separately, to indicate price per person and to specify whether they ate in, took away or ordered delivery.

Detail works both ways

Separate scores reveal exactly where the problem lies. A trattoria in Bologna with excellent food scores but weak service ratings has a staffing issue, not a kitchen issue. Photos uploaded by guests carry as much weight as text: a badly lit plate or a crowded dining room can shape expectations more than the star rating itself.

Volume and seasonality

Restaurants in tourist areas can receive dozens of reviews a week in summer and very few in winter. Rating swings therefore follow the calendar, and a single bad weekend in August, with an overstretched team, can leave a trace that lasts the whole year if nothing balances it out.

Recurring complaint patterns

Most negative Google restaurant reviews fall into a handful of predictable categories. Recognising them helps decide quickly whether a review should be reported, answered or used as feedback for the team.

  • Charges that surprise foreign guests, such as the cover charge (coperto) or bread, even when they are shown on the menu.
  • Waiting times and table turnover during peak hours.
  • Delivery problems caused by the courier or the platform, posted on the restaurant's own profile.
  • Accusations of being a "tourist trap", often based on location rather than the actual meal.
  • Allergen or food-safety claims, which require a careful and documented response.
  • Waves of one-star ratings after a viral social media post, from people who never visited.

The last group, together with reviews from competitors and former staff, usually violates Google's policies on fake engagement or conflicts of interest and has a realistic chance of removal. Our guide to removing fake reviews from Google Maps in Italy explains how to report them effectively.

Extortion-style reviews: when a guest threatens a rating

A guest who demands a refund, a free meal or a discount "or else I'll leave one star" should never be accommodated. Giving in rewards the behaviour, and the review often appears anyway.

The practical response is to document the threat as it happens: write down the time, table and staff present, keep any messages or emails, and preserve receipts and CCTV footage where available and lawful. If the review is then published, report it to Google as a policy violation and send the evidence through Business Profile support, explaining that the content was used as leverage. Google's rules prohibit using reviews to obtain benefits, and a documented sequence of events makes removal far more likely. In serious or repeated cases, threatening reputational damage to obtain an advantage can amount to attempted extortion under Italian criminal law, and a complaint to the Carabinieri or Polizia di Stato creates an official record that also supports the report to Google.

The strongest protection against blackmail reviews is a written record made on the day. Without it, the review looks like any other unhappy customer.

Tourists and locals: two audiences, two kinds of reviews

Tourists and regulars review for different reasons, and replies should take that into account. Visitors judge an experience they will probably never repeat and compare it with expectations shaped at home; locals judge consistency over time and notice small changes in quality or prices.

Reply to foreign guests in the language of their review, because Google's automatic translation can distort tone. When the complaint concerns Italian dining customs, such as the coperto, the absence of cappuccino after dinner or the timing of courses, a short, polite explanation helps future readers more than an apology. Regulars, on the other hand, expect to be recognised; a personal reply that refers to their usual visits shows that the restaurant values loyalty without revealing anything private about them.

How to answer the main types of review

Every reply is written for future guests as much as for the reviewer, so it should be brief, factual and free of arguments. The approach depends on the nature of the review.

Type of reviewReply approach
Fair criticism of food or serviceThank, acknowledge the specific point, state what has changed
Price or coperto complaintExplain calmly where prices are displayed, without sarcasm
Delivery issueClarify the role of the platform, invite the guest to contact you directly
Suspected fake or extortion reviewReport it first; if you reply, state neutrally that you have no record of the visit
Positive reviewPersonal thanks mentioning a dish or detail, never a copy-and-paste text

More detail on tone and wording is available in our article on answering a negative review without escalating.

Raising the rating sustainably

A rating improves durably only when more satisfied guests leave reviews, and that requires a simple routine built into service rather than occasional campaigns. Effective online review management in a restaurant is mostly a matter of habit.

  1. Create a short review link from your Business Profile and turn it into a QR code on the bill folder or table card.
  2. Train staff to ask at the right moment, typically when a guest compliments the meal, without pressure.
  3. Ask every guest equally; selecting only happy customers or offering a dessert, discount or drink in exchange breaks Google's rules.
  4. Read new reviews daily during high season and reply within a couple of days.
  5. Share recurring complaints with the kitchen and floor team every week, so the causes disappear rather than just the symptoms.
